instructions: Cut the baguette into 4 pieces about 6 inches long. Split each piece lengthwise.

If the bread isn't fresh from the bakery, lay the pieces cut side up on a baking sheet and toast them under the broiler or in a toaster oven for 1 to 2 minutes, until warm and lightly golden. Stay close. The broiler goes from golden to burnt fast.
Meanwhile, pour the milk into a small saucepan and warm it over medium-low heat for about 3 minutes, until steaming. Don't let it boil. Pour it into 4 mugs.
Spread the butter over the cut sides, about 1/2 tbsp on each half, right out to the edges.
Spoon about 1 tbsp of jam onto each buttered half and spread it flat.
Serve with the mugs of warm milk for dipping.
method_notes: Hoodoo Q's tartines are a split baguette, toasted if it isn't fresh, spread with butter and jam, and dipped in warm milk, hot chocolate or coffee; that is the lead and where the method comes from. Bonne Maman's tartine page agrees on thin French bread with unsalted butter and a jam spread but gives no amounts. Neither page has a rating, so this is a fallback lead. Amounts are Pomona's own, sized for four, since neither source gives any.
